title: Free French
capsule: La France Libre was the government-in-exile proclaimed by General Charles de Gaulle in London on 18 June 1940, following France's armistice with Germany, and was recognized by Britain as the legitimate French authority. Rallying French colonial territories — beginning with Equatorial Africa and Cameroon in August 1940 — the Free French Forces participated in campaigns across North Africa, the Levant, and Europe, fielding over 1.3 million soldiers by 1944. On 3 June 1944, the movement reconstituted itself as the French Committee of National Liberation and then as the Provisional Government of the French Republic, formally superseding the Vichy regime after the liberation of Paris in August 1944.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Free French-controlled areas shifted considerably month by month; colonial territory held varies by campaign phase and is well documented in French and British military records, but mapping it as a static polygon is an approximation.
